claim.pdf_says: 14.9.12.4   General rules  (bold run-in heading, one level below '14.9.12 DIVIDE statement', same level as 14.9.12.3 Syntax rules)
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.12.4 General rules   (H2 — while the immediately preceding sibling on page 645 is '### 14.9.12.3 Syntax rules' and the parent is '## 14.9.12 DIVIDE statement')
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect as 14.9.11.4: the General rules block is promoted to sibling-of-the-statement level, breaking the outline and detaching the DIVIDE general rules from the DIVIDE statement. It is also internally inconsistent with 14.9.12.3 two pages earlier, which is correctly H3.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides. PDF: rendered page 646 (printed folio 616) at 300 dpi carries, as its first content line under the running head, the bold heading '14.9.12.4   General rules'. Font extraction (PyMuPDF) shows it as a single span at 11.67 pt Cambria,Bold at y=90 — byte-identical typography to '14.9.12.3   Syntax rules' (page 645, y=491, 11.67 pt Cambria,Bold) and to '14.9.12   DIVIDE statement', '14.9.12.1   General', '14.9.12.2   General formats' (page 644, y=90/116/179, all 11.67 pt Cambria,Bold). The PDF therefore encodes hierarchy solely through clause-number depth, and 14.9.12.4 — a four-component number — is unambiguously a subclause of 14.9.12 and a sibling of 14.9.12.3. MARKDOWN: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 26621 '## 14.9.12 DIVIDE statement' (H2), line 26624 '### 14.9.12.1 General' (H3), line 26629 '### 14.9.12.2 General formats' (H3), line 26727 '### 14.9.12.3 Syntax rules' (H3), line 26744 '## 14.9.12.4 General rules' (H2). The transcription thus makes 14.9.12.4 a sibling of its own parent 14.9.12 and of the peer statements 14.9.11/14.9.13, orphaning the DIVIDE general rules from the DIVIDE statement in every outline, TOC and anchor-hierarchy derived from heading depth. Refutation attempts, all failed: (a) not a missing-text finding — the heading string is present and verbatim correct; (b) not page-break furniture — a page-top-position correlation test over all 204 four-component 14.9.x.y headings shows 48 of the 162 CORRECT H3 headings also sit immediately after a page marker, so page position does not drive the level; (c) not a deliberate convention — H3 is the overwhelming norm (162 of 204), and the H2 promotions are a scattered minority; (d) not reflow, wrapping or hyphenation — this is a discrete heading-depth token. The defect is genuine and machine-checkable.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but mislabeled and slightly misquoted. (1) kind should be 'wrong-heading-level', not 'missing-heading': no text is missing or altered — the heading reads '14.9.12.4 General rules' in both sources, and the general-rules body text on page 646 transcribes faithfully. The defect is purely that the markdown emits it at depth H2 instead of H3. (2) The PDF heading is a bold STANDALONE heading on its own line, not a 'run-in' heading (no body text follows on the same line). (3) 14.9.12.3 Syntax rules is ONE page earlier (page 645), not two. (4) Scope is wider than a pair: this is one instance of a systematic transcription inconsistency — of the 204 four-component 14.9.x.y headings, 42 carry the wrong depth (40 promoted to H2, 2 demoted to H4), including 14.9.1.3/1.4, 14.9.2.3/2.4, 14.9.4.3, 14.9.10.4, 14.9.11.4, 14.9.12.4, and on through 14.9.49.4. Impact is navigational/structural only (outline, TOC, anchor hierarchy, and any tooling that derives ISO clause parentage from markdown heading depth); no normative content is lost. Fix should be a mechanical sweep that sets heading depth from clause-number component count, not a one-line patch at line 26744.
